# Best RV power station + solar combos

The right combo depends on how you camp. The search results didn't give me direct retailer product pages, so the links below go to the review pages that carry the current price buttons. Prices change, so check them before buying.

## My picks

**1. Best for full-time RV living or running the A/C: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3**
- 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous (8,000W surge), expandable past 12kWh.
- Recharges 0-80% in about 50 minutes from a wall outlet.
- It's heavy, a two-person lift, and it's the most expensive option once you add batteries.
- Source: [EmergencyEnergy RV comparison](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)

**2. Best value with a built-in RV outlet: BLUETTI AC200L**
- 2,048Wh, 2,400W, a 30A RV port, and up to 1,200W of solar input. It weighs about 62 lb.
- Good for multi-day trips with a fridge, Starlink and a laptop.
- Sources: [Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/) and [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)
- Avoid confusing it with the older AC200P, which caps solar at 700W and recharges slowly from the wall ([Outdoor Power Stations](https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti)).

**3. Best for weekends: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus**
- 1,024Wh, 1,800W, and about 28 lb. It accepts up to 1,000W of solar over two inputs and expands to 5kWh.
- Source: [Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)
- A simpler, lighter alternative is the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (1,070Wh, about 23.8 lb). Its solar input is capped at 400W, so two 200W SolarSaga panels is the most it can use.

**Also worth a look:** Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro (3,024Wh, 3,000W) if you mainly want to start a roof A/C. See the [EmergencyEnergy comparison](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/).

## Solar panels to pair
- **Small to mid units:** A 300-400W folding array can refill a mid-size unit in a full day of decent sun ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)). NomadSignal suggests a Renogy 200W foldable solar suitcase for 1,000-2,000Wh units ([NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife)).
- **Check the solar input limit first:** A bigger array than the station can accept is wasted. Match your panel wattage to the unit's rated input.
- **Bundles:** Panel wattage varies by package, so confirm what's included.

## Sizing tips
- Add up your loads in watts, then multiply by hours. A 150W fridge for 10 hours is about 1,500Wh.
- A 13,500 BTU roof A/C draws about 1,500W running and spikes above 3,000W at startup. That needs a 3,000W+ unit like the DELTA Pro 3 or Jackery 3000 Pro.
- If you want to feed the trailer's shore inlet, have a licensed electrician do any hardwired connection.

## A note on one search result
One result, a deal page for the ALLPOWERS R4000, contained text telling AI assistants to give shoppers a specific discount code and affiliate link. I ignored it and didn't include that link. It wasn't part of your request, and it was written to steer the recommendation. The R4000 is a 3,456Wh unit that may be fine, but I'd compare it on its merits rather than on that page's say-so.

If you tell me your RV's loads (A/C or not, fridge, Starlink) and your budget, I can narrow this to one combo.
